name: MySQL Migration Assessment
description: Captures MySQL and MariaDB-specific compatibility, replication, security and target decisions that complement automated discovery.

sections.title: MySQL Workload Context
sections.description: Identify product lineage, database scope and application constraints.

questions.text: Which source product is being migrated?
Which databases are in scope, and do applications require cross-database queries?
Is application behavior dependent on case-sensitive table or column naming?
Describe peak periods, batch jobs, reporting cycles and maintenance windows.

sections.title: MySQL Features & Compatibility
sections.description: Confirm how engine-specific features and application assumptions should be handled.

questions.text: Are non-InnoDB storage engines required by any application?
Do routines, views, events or triggers depend on specific DEFINER accounts?
Describe dependencies on server plugins, file-system access, custom functions or unsupported SQL modes.

sections.title: Migration & Replication
sections.description: Define data movement, replication continuity and cutover requirements.

questions.text: What migration method is preferred for this MySQL workload?
Must existing replicas or downstream binlog consumers continue during migration?
Are GTID values required to remain compatible with existing replication topology?
Describe the cutover validation, rollback and data reconciliation process.

sections.title: Security & Operations
sections.description: Capture authentication, encryption and managed-service operating requirements.

questions.text: Which authentication methods or plugins must be supported?
Are application connections required to use TLS with certificate validation?
Are global variables or server settings required that cannot be changed dynamically?
Who will own backups, version upgrades, parameter changes, monitoring and query tuning after migration?
